A specific framework choice, with the reasoning behind it and backed by 2026 benchmarks, before any build begins.

If your project doesn't need the complexity of one framework, I'll say so, including when a single framework suffices.

sec-head.h2: What is LangChain? What is LlamaIndex?

p: LangChain, via LangGraph, excels at multi-step agent orchestration with stateful graphs, while LlamaIndex focuses on fast, efficient retrieval with hierarchical indexing. Both are MIT-licensed, but by 2026 the critical distinction is latency and memory overhead: LlamaIndex retrieval is ~6ms overhead versus LangGraph's ~14ms, making LlamaIndex ideal for retrieval-heavy RAG and LangGraph for agentic workflows with complex tool use. The real decision between LangChain and LlamaIndex hinges on whether your core bottleneck is retrieval speed or agent orchestration.

td: Multi-step agent orchestration via LangGraph graphs, stateful loops, and tool integration
Fast hierarchical retrieval with low overhead (~6ms), advanced chunking, and query synthesis
Complex agentic workflows where RAG is one of many tools, requiring state and orchestration
Retrieval-heavy applications demanding low latency and high recall, e.g., document Q&A, knowledge bases
30-40% less code for standard RAG pipelines due to native indexing abstractions
500+ integrations, LangSmith observability, mature agent tooling
300+ connectors, LlamaParse for advanced document parsing, growing agent support
Typically requires third-party tracing (e.g., Arize, Weights & Biases)

p: In production, the 2026 standard is a hybrid: LlamaIndex handles ingestion, hierarchical indexing, and fast retrieval, while LangGraph orchestrates multi-step agent logic with state and tools. I build this architecture when a project demands both retrieval speed and complex orchestration—otherwise I choose just one to avoid unnecessary overhead.
